requirements.forbidden_behavior: The implementation must not require each message to complete before another message can use the connection.

requirements.condition: When HTTP fields are encoded for HTTP/2 transport.

requirements.why_checkable: Encoded HTTP fields can be inspected to determine whether the protocol's field-coding mechanism is used.

requirements.quote:
HTTP/2 addresses these issues by defining an optimized mapping of
   HTTP's semantics to an underlying connection.  Specifically, it
   allows interleaving of messages on the same connection and uses an
   efficient coding for HTTP fields.  It also allows prioritization of
   requests, letting more important requests complete more quickly,
   further improving performance.
requirements.condition: When requests are assigned differing priorities.
requirements.required_behavior: The implementation permits requests to be prioritized.
requirements.why_checkable: An implementation interface and its wire behavior can be tested for support of request prioritization.

requirements.quote:
Finally, HTTP/2 also enables more efficient processing of messages
   through use of binary message framing.
requirements.condition: When HTTP/2 messages are transmitted or received.
requirements.required_behavior: The implementation uses binary message framing.
requirements.why_checkable: Wire output and input parsing can be checked for binary frame-based representation.

requirements.quote:
HTTP/2 provides an optimized transport for HTTP semantics.  HTTP/2
   supports all of the core features of HTTP but aims to be more
   efficient than HTTP/1.1.
requirements.condition: When implementing HTTP/2.
requirements.required_behavior: The implementation supports all core features of HTTP.
requirements.why_checkable: Feature tests can determine whether the implementation exposes the core HTTP semantics, though the exact feature set is defined outside this chunk.

requirements.quote:
HTTP/2 is a connection-oriented application-layer protocol that runs
   over a TCP connection ([TCP]).  The client is the TCP connection
   initiator.
requirements.condition: When establishing a direct HTTP/2 transport described by this protocol overview.
requirements.required_behavior: The HTTP/2 protocol runs over a TCP connection.
requirements.why_checkable: Connection setup can be observed to verify that HTTP/2 traffic is carried over TCP.

requirements.quote:
HTTP/2 is a connection-oriented application-layer protocol that runs
   over a TCP connection ([TCP]).  The client is the TCP connection
   initiator.
requirements.condition: When an HTTP/2 TCP connection is established.
requirements.required_behavior: The client initiates the TCP connection.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The server must not be treated as the TCP connection initiator.
requirements.why_checkable: Connection traces identify which endpoint initiated the TCP connection and which endpoint acts as the HTTP/2 client.

requirements.condition: When HTTP/2 protocol data is encoded or parsed.
requirements.required_behavior: The implementation represents the basic protocol unit as a frame.
requirements.why_checkable: The implementation's wire encoder and parser can be checked for frame-based protocol units.

requirements.quote:
Multiplexing of requests is achieved by having each HTTP request/
   response exchange associated with its own stream (Section 5).
requirements.condition: When multiplexing HTTP request/response exchanges.
requirements.required_behavior: Each HTTP request/response exchange is associated with its own stream.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Distinct request/response exchanges must not be assigned as one exchange to the same stream.
requirements.why_checkable: Stream identifiers and decoded request/response exchanges can be correlated in protocol traces.

requirements.quote:
Streams are largely independent of each other, so a blocked or
   stalled request or response does not prevent progress on other
   streams.
requirements.condition: When a request or response on one stream is blocked or stalled.
requirements.required_behavior: Other streams remain able to make progress.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: A blocked or stalled request or response must not prevent progress on other streams.
requirements.why_checkable: A runtime test can stall one stream and observe whether traffic on another stream continues.

requirements.quote:
Effective use of multiplexing depends on flow control and
   prioritization.  Flow control (Section 5.2) ensures that it is
   possible to efficiently use multiplexed streams by restricting data
   that is transmitted to what the receiver is able to handle.
requirements.condition: When transmitting flow-controlled data on multiplexed streams.
requirements.required_behavior: The implementation restricts transmitted data to what the receiver is able to handle.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The implementation must not transmit flow-controlled data beyond what the receiver is able to handle.
requirements.why_checkable: Tests can advertise bounded receiver capacity and compare transmitted data quantities with the resulting flow-control allowance.

requirements.quote:
Prioritization (Section 5.3) ensures that limited resources are used
   most effectively.  This revision of HTTP/2 deprecates the priority
   signaling scheme from [RFC7540].
requirements.condition: When considering use of the priority signaling scheme defined by RFC 7540.
requirements.why_checkable: The passage says the old scheme is deprecated but does not state a concrete required or forbidden implementation behavior in this chunk.

requirements.quote:
Because HTTP fields used in a connection can contain large amounts of
   redundant data, frames that contain them are compressed
   (Section 4.3).  This has especially advantageous impact upon request
requirements.condition: When a frame contains HTTP fields.
requirements.required_behavior: The frame's HTTP fields are compressed.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: HTTP fields in such a frame must not be emitted using an uncompressed field representation.
requirements.why_checkable: Frames containing fields can be captured and decoded to verify use of the HTTP/2 field-compression representation.

requirements.quote:
Finally, HTTP/2 adds a new, optional interaction mode whereby a
   server can push responses to a client (Section 8.4).  This is
requirements.condition: When the optional server-push interaction mode is implemented and used.
requirements.required_behavior: The server can push responses to the client.
requirements.why_checkable: A server configured for push can be exercised to determine whether it initiates a pushed response.

requirements.quote:
network usage against a potential latency gain.  The server does this
   by synthesizing a request, which it sends as a PUSH_PROMISE frame.
requirements.condition: When a server initiates an HTTP/2 pushed response.
requirements.required_behavior: The server synthesizes a request and sends it as a PUSH_PROMISE frame.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The server must not initiate the described push without representing the synthetic request in a PUSH_PROMISE frame.
requirements.why_checkable: A server-push trace can be checked for a PUSH_PROMISE carrying the synthetic request.

requirements.quote:
The server is then able to send a response to the synthetic request
   on a separate stream.
requirements.condition: When the server sends the response associated with a pushed synthetic request.
requirements.required_behavior: The response is sent on a stream separate from the stream carrying the associated push promise.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The pushed response must not be sent as the response exchange of the stream carrying the associated push promise.
requirements.why_checkable: The stream identifier of the PUSH_PROMISE and that of the pushed response can be compared in a protocol trace.

requirements.quote:
All numeric values are in network byte order.  Values are unsigned
   unless otherwise indicated.  Literal values are provided in decimal
   or hexadecimal as appropriate.  Hexadecimal literals are prefixed
   with "0x" to distinguish them from decimal literals.
requirements.condition: When encoding or decoding a multibyte numeric value defined by the specification.
requirements.required_behavior: The implementation uses network byte order.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The implementation must not encode or interpret such values in host or little-endian byte order.
requirements.why_checkable: Known multibyte values can be encoded and decoded and their byte ordering inspected.

requirements.quote:
All numeric values are in network byte order.  Values are unsigned
   unless otherwise indicated.  Literal values are provided in decimal
   or hexadecimal as appropriate.  Hexadecimal literals are prefixed
   with "0x" to distinguish them from decimal literals.
requirements.condition: When processing a numeric value for which the specification does not explicitly indicate signedness.
requirements.required_behavior: The implementation treats the value as unsigned.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The implementation must not interpret the value as signed unless the specification indicates otherwise.
requirements.why_checkable: Boundary values with the high bit set can be used to distinguish unsigned from signed interpretation.

requirements.quote:
This specification describes binary formats using the conventions
   described in Section 1.3 of RFC 9000 [QUIC].  Note that this format
   uses network byte order and that high-valued bits are listed before
   low-valued bits.
requirements.condition: When interpreting binary format diagrams in the specification.
requirements.required_behavior: The implementation interprets multibyte values in network byte order and maps listed high-valued bits before low-valued bits.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The implementation must not reverse the specified byte or bit significance ordering.
requirements.why_checkable: Test vectors with asymmetric byte and bit patterns can reveal reversed byte or bit interpretation.

requirements.quote:
client:  The endpoint that initiates an HTTP/2 connection.  Clients
      send HTTP requests and receive HTTP responses.
requirements.condition: When an endpoint acts as the HTTP/2 client.
requirements.required_behavior: The endpoint initiates the HTTP/2 connection, sends HTTP requests, and receives HTTP responses.
requirements.why_checkable: Connection establishment and message-direction traces can verify all three client-role behaviors.

requirements.quote:
connection error:  An error that affects the entire HTTP/2
      connection.
requirements.condition: When an error is classified as a connection error.
requirements.required_behavior: The error affects the entire HTTP/2 connection.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The implementation must not confine a connection error's effect to only one stream.
requirements.error_behavior: Apply the error at connection scope.
requirements.why_checkable: Injecting a condition classified as a connection error can verify whether its handling is scoped to the whole connection rather than one stream.
